oneSentenceSummary: Cartier UK sales exceeded £250 million while Pragnell faced a profit squeeze despite record sales of £100.5 million.
introParagraph: Cartier reports UK sales exceeding £250 million, reflecting strong demand in the luxury sector.  In contrast, Pragnell experiences a profit squeeze despite achieving record sales of £100. 5 million.
editorialTake:
Profit growth in luxury and jewellery is now decoupling from sales growth, and the culprit is not just inflation or tariffs, it is the new cost of competing in an AI-powered, logistics-driven market. Cartier UK posted record sales of £251 million and grew operating profit by 25 percent, but Pragnell and Laings both saw profit margins shrink despite hitting all-time sales highs. Pragnell’s profit fell 11 percent and Laings’ dropped over 40 percent, even as both grew top-line revenue. The difference is not just brand equity or product mix. It is about who can adapt fastest to new operating realities.

Visa’s data shows US holiday retail spending up 4.2 percent, but that growth is being shaped by AI tools that change how shoppers discover and compare products. Zero-click searches and AI-driven shopping journeys, as reported by Practical Ecommerce, mean brands have less control over how they get found and more pressure to win in the moments that matter. Meanwhile, Amazon’s massive new investments in AI and data centers are raising the bar for what it costs to deliver seamless, fast, and personalized ecommerce. The winners are those who can keep up with both the technology arms race and the shifting cost structure of last-mile delivery, as seen in the expansion of Instacart, DoorDash, and Uber Eats partnerships.

Some will say luxury is immune to these pressures, that brand power and heritage shield margins from the churn of retail tech. But the numbers at Pragnell and Laings say otherwise. Rising costs and new consumer expectations are eating into profits, even as sales climb. Only those who adapt their operations, not just their marketing, will avoid the squeeze.

For luxury and jewellery operators, the next quarter is about ruthless focus: audit every step from product discovery to delivery. Invest in AI tools that actually drive conversion and retention, not just buzz. And scrutinize fulfillment partnerships for hidden costs. Margin protection now means mastering the new math of digital retail, not just selling more.
